page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by the 3.3 GHz ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processor. The system provides 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating simultaneous multithreading contention. Cache provisioning includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core, alongside 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Integrated hardware includes 1900 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 17 Gbps baseline network connection. The platform contains no dedicated GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application-level testing, the configuration exhibits strong multi-core processing capabilities, scoring 25006.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 62134.0 in Geekbench Clang software compilation, both situated within the top 10% tier. Compression throughput is also strong, achieving 36.47 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 17.32 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Database operations measure in the top tier at 45874.73 ops on PassMark, supported by a 4272.72 GB/sec cached memory read score and strong Redis SET throughput of 94.77 million operations per second. Tradeoffs are present in large uncached memory transfers (174.43 GB/sec read and 81.64 GB/sec write) and CPU-based large language model inference, both ranking within mid-tier percentiles. The combination of dedicated ARM cores and direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high resource efficiency for transactional databases, CI/CD build farms, caching clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with 32 dedicated physical cores (32 vCPUs) built on the 3.3 GHz ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 architecture. It pairs 128.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core) with 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a 17 Gbps baseline network interface, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight exceptional performance in software compilation, Geekbench multi-core and single-core evaluation, and PassMark database operations, all placing within the top 10%. Memory-cached operations and single-threaded compression throughput also score at top levels, while uncached bandwidth and CPU-based machine learning inference show average performance. The instance provides an efficient compute-to-storage architecture well suited for relational and key-value databases, distributed caching layers, web serving platforms, and software build pipelines requiring fast direct-attached NVMe storage.
